faqs.question: Is an opening range the opening price?
faqs.answer: No. The opening price is one observation; the range is the high–low interval over a declared window.

faqs.question: When is the morning range complete?
faqs.answer: For the 09:30–10:00 convention, after the final candle covering that interval completes.

faqs.question: Should I use fixed EST all year?
faqs.answer: Use America/New_York so the date determines daylight saving.

faqs.question: Does a range break guarantee continuation?
faqs.answer: No. Compare acceptance outside, rejection back inside and unresolved outcomes.

faqs.question: Does the stock-market calendar apply to every futures session?
faqs.answer: No. Check the actual instrument, session template, holiday and early-close rules.

faqs.question: Is an RTH gap the first half-hour range?
faqs.answer: No. It compares the prior selected regular-session close with the next regular-session open.

faqs.question: How is a gap midpoint calculated?
faqs.answer: Add its lower and upper boundaries and divide by two. For 100–108, the midpoint is 104.

faqs.question: Must NWOG fill during the week?
faqs.answer: No. A weekly gap can be partly tested, crossed or left unvisited.

faqs.question: Is a chart close the official settlement?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. A last bar, a session close and an exchange settlement can differ.

faqs.question: Can different FX feeds show different gaps?
faqs.answer: Yes. Broker quotes and session boundaries differ; use one documented feed consistently.

faqs.question: Can a real FVG be rejected by the first-presented model?
faqs.answer: Yes. A gap can satisfy outer-wick geometry yet remain inside the preceding balanced area.

faqs.question: Is every 09:30 FVG eligible?
faqs.answer: No. The advanced treatment adds opening and liquidity context; it is not the basic 09:31 selection rule.

faqs.question: When can I confirm the third candle?
faqs.answer: After it closes. Its timestamp is not the time its final high and low became available.

faqs.question: Does touching the near edge fill a CE order?
faqs.answer: No. A 104–106 gap has CE 105; a low of 105.5 has not reached that midpoint.

faqs.question: Does first mean highest probability?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. Qualification, execution and results need a defined sample rather than a label.

faqs.question: Are twenty trading days twenty calendar days?
faqs.answer: No. Count completed trading sessions; weekends and market closures are not additional trading days.

faqs.question: Does premium mean fundamentally overvalued?
faqs.answer: No. Here it means above the midpoint of a declared range.

faqs.question: Is suspension identical to a classic FVG?
faqs.answer: No. The body-gap configuration can include wick overlap that would fail the classic outer-wick test.

faqs.question: Can I switch lookbacks whenever a setup fails?
faqs.answer: Not in a consistent test. Declare extensions and their conditions before seeing the outcome.

faqs.question: Does an overlapping BPR guarantee a reaction?
faqs.answer: No. Overlap is geometry; relevance, failure rules and execution remain separate.

faqs.question: Should SMT compare a high with a closing price?
faqs.answer: Not for a high-based test. Compare corresponding highs; define a close-based test separately.

faqs.question: Can SMT disappear?
faqs.answer: Yes. The lagging market can later exceed its own anchor within the comparison window.

faqs.question: Do NQ and ES need the same numerical price?
faqs.answer: No. Compare each instrument with its own corresponding anchor, not with the other instrument’s price.

faqs.question: Is DXY always the inverse of EUR/USD?
faqs.answer: No. An inverse relationship is conditional, and the comparison convention must be stated.

faqs.question: Is SMT enough to execute a trade?
faqs.answer: No. It supplies context; entry, failure, objective and execution assumptions are separate.

faqs.question: Is every old-high break a liquidity sweep reversal?
faqs.answer: No. Price can continue and accept above it; study the response rather than the break alone.

faqs.question: Can candles prove the stops were there?
faqs.answer: No. A visible extreme is observable; hidden resting stops are an inference.

faqs.question: Is a rejection-block body the full wick?
faqs.answer: No. Label the chosen opening/closing boundary separately from the wick extreme.

faqs.question: What if the deferred return never arrives?
faqs.answer: Record an unfilled idea. Do not move the entry retrospectively to claim participation.

faqs.question: Is every FVG overlap the Gauntlet?
faqs.answer: No. The reviewed example selects a particular SIBI and body-gap reference within a breaker-related leg.

faqs.question: Is Venom simply a ninety-minute cycle?
faqs.answer: No. This variant uses a particular 08:00–09:30 pre-open range and a defined subsequent response.

faqs.question: Does a wick above the high meet the reviewed bearish close condition?
faqs.answer: No. The reviewed version includes a candle close above the selected buy-side reference.

faqs.question: What are the two fangs?
faqs.answer: Opposing inefficient departures assessed after the selected excursion, not two arbitrary candles.

faqs.question: Is a deferred entry guaranteed?
faqs.answer: No. Price can move toward the objective without returning to the chosen entry boundary.

faqs.question: Must every Venom include SMT and a breaker?
faqs.answer: Do not impose an unsupported universal chain. State the exact variant and any additional study filters.

faqs.question: Which post-10:00 swing matters after a morning decline?
faqs.answer: The first confirmed prominent swing high after 10:00 is a reference in the studied retracement variant.

faqs.question: Must lunch reverse the morning?
faqs.answer: No. Continued expansion and failure to develop the required response are valid contrasting cases.

faqs.question: Do morning arrays flip at 13:30 automatically?
faqs.answer: No. A changed role needs the declared contextual evidence, not just a clock time.

faqs.question: What is the afternoon opening study window?
faqs.answer: The convention used here is 13:30–14:00 New York local time.

faqs.question: Is the MOC study window an exchange rule?
faqs.answer: No. Verify the product’s actual closing process and calendar separately.

faqs.question: Does an FOMC statement settle the whole afternoon?
faqs.answer: No. A later press conference is a separate event and can extend or reverse the first move.

faqs.question: Can one candle tell which of stop and target came first?
faqs.answer: Not when both levels lie within its range. Finer sequence data or a declared ambiguity rule is required.

faqs.question: Does a stop-market guarantee the stop price?
faqs.answer: No. It can slip; a stop-limit has a different risk of remaining unfilled.

faqs.question: Is there a universally safe post-news waiting time?
faqs.answer: No. Define the study rule and execution conditions for the instrument and event.

faqs.question: Should excluded winners be kept in the journal?
faqs.answer: Yes. A filter removes opportunities as well as losses; preserve both to evaluate it fairly.

faqs.question: Are there twelve guaranteed weekly scripts?
faqs.answer: No. Profiles organise conditional scenarios; they do not dictate the day of the final extreme.

faqs.question: Can Monday’s plan use the final weekly high?
faqs.answer: No. That high is only known later; use completed references and provisional scenarios.

faqs.question: Must Friday retrace the week?
faqs.answer: No. A strong trend can continue into the close, including at all-time highs.

faqs.question: Is a new all-time high a ceiling?
faqs.answer: No. Missing old highs above price does not prevent further expansion.

faqs.question: Does weekly premium justify an immediate short?
faqs.answer: No. Range-relative location is context; a separate intraday setup is still required.

faqs.question: Are SPX options settled by delivering shares?
faqs.answer: No. SPX options are cash-settled and European-style; check the particular series and settlement timing.

faqs.question: Is premium received the maximum loss on an uncovered call?
faqs.answer: No. The gain is capped at the premium; rising-price losses have no fixed upper bound.

faqs.question: Can the direction be right and the option still lose?
faqs.answer: Yes. Strike, premium, timing and contract terms matter in addition to direction.

faqs.question: Is a spread’s expiry payoff the full risk picture?
faqs.answer: No. Interim margin, liquidity, execution and product-specific exercise mechanics also matter.

faqs.question: Are the 100/105 examples actual SPX quotes?
faqs.answer: No. They use invented prices to make the arithmetic transparent and are not recommendations.

faqs.question: Is a correct directional idea automatically a win?
faqs.answer: No. A declared entry must be reached after recognition, and the later sequence must be resolved.

faqs.question: Should I edit a prediction after replay?
faqs.answer: Keep the original decision and add a separate review note. Otherwise the journal loses its evidence.

faqs.question: Can all 2025 examples be forced into one model?
faqs.answer: No. The collection includes different approaches; identify the precise model and variant you study.

faqs.question: How should an unresolved candle be counted?
faqs.answer: Keep it unresolved or apply a predeclared conservative assumption, never a convenient target-first guess.

faqs.question: Was every minute of the supplied library verified?
faqs.answer: No. The review uses selected passages from 75 captioned sources and visual review of eight other recordings.
